# trix

> trix is a free, open-source terminal workspace for AI coding agents. It runs Claude Code, Codex, Grok, OpenCode, Cursor, GitHub Copilot CLI, Muse Code, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Amp, shells or any CLI agent side by side, and shows at a glance which one is working, which one needs you and which one has finished. It's written in Rust, MIT licensed, and runs on Linux and macOS (x86_64 and ARM). There is no Windows build.

Generic terminal multiplexers such as tmux and zellij know nothing about agents. trix starts each agent itself and gets live state from it through the agent's own hooks or plugins, without editing the agent's config files:

- When an agent needs you (a permission request or a question), a red strip covers the pane you're in, and you get a desktop notification and a bell. `alt+a` jumps to the agent that has waited longest.
- `alt+g` shows up to four agents side by side, updating live.
- Each agent can work in its own git worktree on its own branch, so parallel agents never overwrite each other's files.
- `alt+v` reviews an agent's diff; from there you can send notes back to it, commit, push, open a pull request and merge.
- For Claude and Codex, each pane shows how full the context window is and what the agent has cost.
- Agents run in a background server: close the terminal and they keep working. After a crash or reboot, each one resumes its conversation.
- `trix spawn`, `send`, `read`, `wait` and `close` let a script, or another agent, run agents.

Install with Homebrew on macOS or Linux: `brew install leofle/trix/trix`. On Arch Linux or Omarchy, install the pacman package from the latest release. Then run `trix claude` (or `trix codex`, and so on) in a project folder.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/leofle/trix#readme): the full documentation
- [Install](https://github.com/leofle/trix#install): Homebrew, pacman, release binaries and building from source
- [Quick start](https://github.com/leofle/trix#quick-start): first steps
- [Keys](https://github.com/leofle/trix#keys): every key binding (all on `alt`)
- [Supported agents](https://github.com/leofle/trix#supported-agents): how each agent reports its state, and how trix resumes it
- [macOS](https://github.com/leofle/trix#macos): making Option send Alt, and other differences from Linux
- [Codex](https://github.com/leofle/trix#codex): the one-time hook trust step
- [Agent control](https://github.com/leofle/trix#agent-control): commands for scripts and agents that run other agents
- [Security](https://github.com/leofle/trix#security): what trix does and doesn't do on your behalf
